questions.question: A company fine-tuned a Foundation Model on Amazon Bedrock using training data that includes confidential information. How can the company ensure the model's responses do not contain this confidential information?

options.text: The company should mask the confidential information from the model responses by leveraging Amazon Bedrock Guardrails

explanation.summary: Bedrock Guardrails can filter sensitive data from model outputs.
explanation.why: Amazon Bedrock Guardrails are designed to detect and block sensitive information in generated responses.

options.text: The company should use encryption to protect the confidential information in the model responses

explanation.summary: Encryption does not control generated output content.
explanation.why: Encryption protects data at rest and in transit, not model-generated responses.

options.text: The company should delete the customized model, remove confidential information from the training data, and fine-tune the model again

explanation.summary: This does not address runtime response filtering.
explanation.why: Model retraining changes training data but does not provide output filtering controls.

options.text: The company should swap Amazon Bedrock with Amazon SageMaker and rebuild the model using Amazon SageMaker built-in algorithms

explanation.summary: Changing services does not solve output filtering.
explanation.why: Output control is independent of the ML platform and requires filtering mechanisms.

questions.question: A security company is evaluating Amazon Rekognition. Which of the following use cases is NOT the right fit for Amazon Rekognition?

explanation.why: Amazon Rekognition provides facial analysis and comparison capabilities.

options.text: Enable multilingual user experiences in your applications

explanation.summary: Rekognition does not provide language translation.
explanation.why: Amazon Rekognition focuses on image and video analysis, not text translation.
Amazon Rekognition includes a built-in celebrity recognition feature.
Amazon Rekognition provides labels and metadata to index media content.

questions.question: A retail company has product catalogs as PDFs and wants to provide current, relevant responses to customer inquiries through its LLM chatbot on Amazon Bedrock. Which approach is most cost-effective?

explanation.summary: RAG avoids retraining and uses external data at runtime.
explanation.why: RAG retrieves relevant data at inference time instead of embedding it in the model.

options.text: Fine-tune the LLM with PDF data

explanation.summary: Fine-tuning is more costly and less flexible.
explanation.why: Fine-tuning requires retraining for updates instead of dynamic retrieval.

options.text: Attach all PDFs to every query

explanation.summary: This increases token usage and cost.
explanation.why: Large prompt sizes increase inference cost and latency.

options.text: Attach a single PDF to each query

explanation.summary: Manual selection does not scale efficiently.
explanation.why: RAG automates retrieval instead of relying on manual document selection.

questions.question: What is a key difference between Foundation Models (FMs) and Large Language Models (LLMs)?

options.text: LLMs are pre-trained, FMs are not

explanation.why: Foundation Models are defined as pre-trained models on large datasets.

options.text: FMs are for text only, LLMs are multimodal

explanation.why: Foundation Models can be multimodal, while LLMs focus on text.

options.text: FMs are general-purpose, LLMs specialize in language

explanation.summary: LLMs are a subset of FMs focused on text.
explanation.why: Foundation Models provide broad capabilities while LLMs focus on NLP tasks.
AWS provides Foundation Models for production use via Bedrock.

questions.question: In generative AI, what is the concept representing discrete units of text?

explanation.summary: Vectors represent numerical values, not text units.
explanation.why: Vectors are mathematical representations, not raw text units.

explanation.summary: Tokens are the discrete text units processed by models.
explanation.why: Tokens represent words, subwords, or characters in model input/output.

explanation.summary: Context window refers to token limits.
explanation.why: Context window defines how many tokens can be processed at once.

explanation.summary: Embeddings are vector representations of text.
explanation.why: Embeddings convert tokens into numerical vectors for processing.

questions.question: A company is comparing Amazon Q and Amazon Bedrock for AI-driven tasks. Which statements correctly describe the differences?

options.text: With Amazon Q, you can choose the underlying Foundation Model. However, Amazon Bedrock does not allow you to choose the underlying Foundation Model

questions.question: A company is using generative AI to create custom reports. What are the key constituents of a good prompting technique?

options.text: Instructions, Hyperparameters, Input data, Output Indicator

options.text: Hyperparameters, Context, Input data, Output Indicator

options.text: Instructions, Parameters, Input data, Output Indicator

explanation.summary: Parameters is not a defined prompt component.
explanation.why: AWS defines prompt components as instructions, context, input data, and output indicator.

options.text: Instructions, Context, Input data, Output Indicator

explanation.summary: This matches AWS prompt design guidance.
explanation.why: Effective prompts include instructions, context, input data, and output indicators.

questions.question: A shopping mall's AI system flags individuals from a specific ethnic group disproportionately. What type of bias is this?

explanation.summary: This relates to subjective human labeling.
explanation.why: Observer bias arises from human interpretation errors, not sampling issues.
